title: Hill AFB Hazardous Waste Removal and Disposal
description: THE INTENT OF THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS TO IDENTIFY QUALIFIED SMALL BUSINESSES, including 8(a), HUBZone, woman-owned, and service-disabled veteran-owned small businesses, for the requirement described below. The intent of this Sources Sought is to identify capable small businesses that can perform with limitations on subcontracting. The scope of work requires the transportation and disposal of Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA) Hazardous wastes, non-RCRA wastes, Batteries, Corrosive waste, Compressed Gas Cylinders, Flammable waste, Demil-required waste, State-Regulated waste, Non-Hazardous Waste, Polychlorinated Biphenyls (PCBs), AFFF and other Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS)-related waste, Mandatory Recycling waste, Reactive waste, and Toxic waste in and around Hill AFB, Utah. In addition, special services will be required such as sampling and analysis, industrial cleaning services, lab packs/loose packs, rolloff box rentals, vacuum box rentals, FRAC Tank rentals, and expedited removals and performance. All services necessary for the collection, storage, processing, removal, transportation, final treatment, and disposal of waste must be in accordance with all local, state, Department of Defense, and Federal laws and regulations. In a set aside, FAR 52.219-14 Limitations on Subcontracting (FEB 2023) (DEVIATION 2021-O0008) states the small business Offeror/Contractor agrees to not pay more than 50% of the amount paid by the Government for contract performance to subcontractors that are not similarly situated entities. Note: The FAR references in the clause above are not aligned with the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (see DEVIATION 2026-O0038); therefore, the following is provided for clarification purposes: references to 19.8 is now 19.105, 9.13 is now 19.106, 19.14 is now 19.107, 19.15 is now 19.108, 8.405-5 is now 8.4, and 16.505(b)(2)(i)(F) is now 16.5. In accordance with 13 CFR � 125.6(h), contractors may be subject to a minimum $500,000 fine if awarded a contract with this clause and does not meet the requirement. DLA has identified the majority of RCRA TSDFs (Treatment, Storage, Disposal Facilities) in the industry as large businesses. All TSDFs used during the performance of this contract must be approved and listed on the Qualified Facilities List located at the following website: https://www.dla.mil/DispositionServices/Offers/Disposal/HazardousWaste/HazWasteDisposal/. Given there is a lack of small business ownership of TSDFs and that disposal costs make up a large portion of the contract dollar value, there is a reasonable probability that a small business would pay more than 50% of the cost of the contract to large businesses. *The Government intends to solicit proposals on SAM.gov and award a commercial Firm-Fixed Priced, Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Services Contract. The contract is anticipated to have one 30-month base period, followed by one 30-month option period. There is no solicitation available at this time. However, attached is a DRAFT Price Schedule and DRAFT Performance Work Statement (PWS) that entities responding to this Sources Sought should use to help determine if they would be able to meet the Limitations on Subcontracting requirements. IF YOUR ENTITY IS CAPABLE OF PERFORMING THE REQUESTED SERVICES, WITHOUT THE LIMITATIONS ON SUBCONTRACTING, THE CAPABILITIES PACKAGE DETAILED BELOW IS NOT REQUIRED. In accordance with FAR 6.101(a) (DEVIATION 2026-O0017 Revision 2), with certain limited exceptions, contracting officers must obtain full and open competition by using competitive procedures to solicit offers and award Government contracts. If your entity would like to respond to this Sources Sought, but is unable to meet the limitations on subcontracting, please email lacie.kaiser@dla.mil with �SOURCES SOUGHT HAZ] HILL� in the subject line, stating your entity�s Notification of Interest (a capabilities package is not required). SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS: Interested entities must demonstrate their ability to perform the requested services, described above, by submitting a brief capabilities package (no more than three pages in length, single-spaced, 12-point font minimum). This documentation must identify, at a minimum: (1) Company name, office location(s), Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), CAGE Code, and a statement identifying small business category(ies) and current status of the small business classification; (2) Relevant experience within the last five years, including any contract number(s), names of individuals responsible for the referenced contracts/projects, and current telephone numbers for those individuals; if you were a subcontractor, identify the work you actually performed as the sub-contractor; and (3) If a small business, a statement identifying your entity�s ability to perform in accordance with FAR 52.219-14 Limitations on Subcontracting (FEB 2023) (DEVIATION 2021-O0008), as well as an explanation of how you would be able to comply with this requirement considering the disposal requirements within the draft price schedule that is anticipated to be included in the contract. (4) A listing of TSDFs your entity would use during the performance of this contract, identifying each TSDF as similarly situated or not as your entity. The submittal package must be emailed to lacie.kaiser@dla.mil with �SOURCES SOUGHT HAZ WASTE HILL� in the subject line. The submittal package must be received no later than 4:30pm Eastern Time, November 12, 2026. Any submission after the specified time and date will not be considered unless it is received before the review of other submissions has started and the Contracting Officer determines that accepting the late submission would not unduly delay the acquisition. Upon review of industry response to this Sources Sought, the Government will determine whether a set-aside acquisition is in the Government's best interest. If an unrestricted solicitation is issued, then the FAR 52.219-14 Limitations on Subcontracting (FEB 2023) (DEVIATION 2021-O0008) would not apply. All responsible entities, including small businesses, are eligible to submit a proposal in response to an unrestricted solicitation. A response to this Sources Sought will not be considered an adequate response to any forthcoming solicitation announcement. The Government WILL NOT provide a debriefing on the results of the survey. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this Sources Sought notice or any follow-up information requests. All information submitted will be held in a confidential manner and will only be used for the purpose intended.

title: Individual Water Treatment Device (IWTD) Laboratory Testing
description: In Cooperation with Product Manager Soldier Clothing and Individual Equipment (PdM SCIE) SECTION 1 - Overview 1.1 Background and Introduction Product Manager Soldier Clothing and Individual Equipment (PdM SCIE) is seeking laboratories to validate the capabilities of Individual Water Treatment Devices (IWTDs). This initiative supports the Department of the Army�s goal of providing potable drinking water for Soldiers from any indigenous fresh water source, which enhances Soldier lethality by reducing load and increasing the duration of autonomous squad-level operations. The Army Contracting Command � Aberdeen Proving Ground (ACC-APG), on behalf of PdM SCIE, is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) to identify laboratories with the required certifications, equipment, and personnel to conduct this validation testing. The information gathered from this RFI will inform a future request for proposal. The Government reserves the right to cancel this opportunity or make no awards in conjunction with this opportunity. The Military Sealift Command (MSC) requires the secure and recurring destruction of non-record, classified/unclassified material marked up to and including SECRET, CONFIDENTIAL, and CUI / FOR OFFICIAL USE ONLY (FOUO). title: Aircraft Pressurized Cabin Leakage Tester (APCLT)
description: SYNOPSIS: #N68335-26-Q-1204 Aircraft Pressurized Cabin Leakage Tester (APCLT) Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division - F/A-18F and EA-18G Royal Australian Air Force (RAAF) Program The Naval Air Warfare Center, Aircraft Division (NAWCAD) Lakehurst, NJ intends to negotiate on a sole source basis with Hydraulics International, Inc. (CAGE: 56529) for the Aircraft Pressurized Cabin Leakage Tester (APCLT) in support of the NAWCAD F/A-18F and EA-18G Royal Australian Air Force (RAAF) Program. This order will procure one (1) APCLT (Part Number (P/N): 4129AS0100-1, National Stock Number (NSN): 4920-01-658-2036). The APCLT is required to check aircraft pressurized cabins and canopy seals for leaks and for the ability to control aircraft cabin pressure. The pneumatic cabin pressure leakage tester will provide the means to meet the requirement and is required by the RAAF. The pneumatic cabin pressure leakage tester is a portable unit that runs on facility supplied compressed air and that can supply various combinations of air flow and air pressure to check leakage and pressure regulation in aircraft cabins and canopy seals. Hydraulics International, Inc., as the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) of the APCLT, is the only source with the requisite knowledge, technical experience, and production-level data to produce these components. The components being procured are integral to check aircraft pressurized cabins and canopy seals for leaks and for the ability to control aircraft cabin pressure and are critical to maintaining operational readiness. The Government intends to solicit and negotiate this requirement under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 2304(c)(1), FAR 6.302-1 - Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. However, the Government will consider all responses received within fifteen days after the date of publication of this synopsis. title: NATO Business Opportunity: Antenna Replacement at Atalanti SATCOM Ground Station
description: The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA) intends to issue a solicitation for one new SATCOM Anchor Station antenna and associated Radome to be installed at Atalanti SATCOM Ground Station in Greece. To bid on this contract, potential U.S. prime contractors must 1) maintain a professionally active facility (office, factory, laboratory, etc.) within the United States, 2) be pre-approved for participation in NATO Competitive Procurement (NCP), 3) be issued a Declaration of Eligibility (DOE) by the Department of Commerce (DOC), and 4) register with NCIA�s eProcurement tool, Neo: https://www.ncia.nato.int/business/procurement/neo-eprocurement The reference for the solicitation is IFB-CO-424392-ARA and all correspondence concerning the solicitation should include this reference. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT The Antenna System shall form part of the SATCOM anchoring component and shall support X-band SATCOM operations. The requirement covers the provision of supplies, installation, integration, and commissioning of a complete SATCOM RF head solution. The solution shall include an antenna with a diameter of at least 11 m, Radome, tracking, transmitting, and receiving subsystems, and all associate civil works and services. The RF-head will be integrated into the Atalanti/Greece SATCOM Anchoring Component and shall include the required electrical, data, IF and monitoring interfaces necessary for full system operation and integration within the existing site infrastructure. Objective: The expected result is a fully installed, integrated, tested, documented and accepted Antenna and Radome installation that: a. Meets the Antenna SRS, Radome and Civil Work SRS; b. Supports X-band SATCOM transmit and receive operation; c. Provides automatic satellite tracking capability; d. Provides environmental protection through a rigid, non-inflatable Radome; e. Provides compliant civil, electrical, grounding, bonding and lightning protection installation; f. Provides verified M&C integration with the site�s monitoring and control environment g. Provides tested safety interlocks, emergency stops, access controls and maintenance provisions; h. Provides complete documentation, including as-built drawings, training, and transition-to-operations support. Key Deliverables: Key deliverables include the RF-head and its associated antenna, tracking, Tx and Rx sub-systems; non-inflatable Radome; required civil and electrical works; IF and M&C cabling; installation and integration activities; service laptop; and complete as-built documentation. The contractor shall also provide all necessary cables, waveguides, connectors, interfaces and installation materials required for a complete operational solution. Final deliverables shall include the relevant interface documentation and as-built drawings covering the installed system and associated infrastructure. The complete solution shall be delivered fully installed, integrated with the existing system, tested, commissioned, and ready for operational use. BECOMING ELIGIBLE TO BID NCP requires that the U.S. Government issue a DOE for potential U.S. prime contractors interested in this project. Before the U.S. Government can do so, however, the U.S. Government must approve the U.S. firm for participation in NCP. U.S. firms are approved for NCP on a facility-by-facility basis. The U.S. NCP application is a one-time application. The application requires supporting documentation in the form of 1) a company resume or capability statement indicating contracts completed as a prime contractor and 2) an annual report or set of financial documents indicating compilation, review, or audit by an independent CPA. U.S. firms can download a copy of the NCP application from the following website: https://www.bis.gov/about-bis/bis-leadership-and-offices/SIES/business-opportunities-nato DOC is the U.S. Government agency that approves NCP applications. Please submit to the email address provided your application and supporting documentation (as attachments). If your firm is interested in a specific NCP project at this time, please also include the following in the TEXT of your email: - the title and/or solicitation number of the project - the name/phone/email of the company employee who should receive the bid documents After approval of your one-time NCP application, DOC will then know to follow up by issuing a DOE for the project. DOC will transmit the DOE to the NATO contracting agency. title: Individual Water Treatment Device (IWTD) for Reduction/Removal of Toxic Industrial Chemicals and Materials
description: In Cooperation with Product Manager Soldier Clothing and Individual Equipment (PdM SCIE) and the US Army Combat Capabilities Development Command (DEVCOM) Soldier Center SECTION 1 - Overview 1.1 Background and Introduction The U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command (DEVCOM) Soldier Center is conducting a market investigation to identify products and technologies for individual Soldier water purification. This effort focuses on capabilities for the reduction or removal of Toxic Industrial Chemicals (TICs) and Toxic Industrial Materials (TIMs) from any indigenous fresh water sources. This Request for Information (RFI) seeks to identify suppliers of water treatment technologies that meet Buy American Act requirements and can be integrated with current and future equipment, such as the Individual Water Treatment Device (IWTD) and MOLLE Hydration System. Information gathered will be used for planning purposes to address military water purification needs. Respondents are encouraged to submit alternative technical approaches or product solutions that vary from the listed specifications, as long as they meet or exceed the core capability requirement. This is a Sources Sought Announcement for information and planning purposes only. It is not a Request for Proposal (RFP) and does not constitute a commitment by the U.S. Government. 1.2 Project Problem Statement The DEVCOM Soldier Center is interested in products and technologies that meet or have the potential to meet the following key performance parameters for individual water purification. Respondents should provide actual, demonstrated product performance for each parameter, including where performance does not meet specifications listed below: Contaminant Removal: Capable of removing TICs and TIMs to levels mandated by the Defense Health Agency (DCPH-A), as detailed in the attached "Toxic Industrial Chemical/Material Military Exposure Guideline." Compatibility: Compatible with standard military canteens and hydration systems. Physical Specifications: Weight: Not to exceed 12 oz. Size: Low bulk and compact. Operational Life: At least 135 liters. Shelf Life: 5-year storage stability with an 18-month unused service life. Environmental Resilience: System will not degrade in temperatures from -33�C to 52�C. Capable of treating water ranging in temperature from above freezing to 52�C (liquid water up to 52�C). Must not be impacted by freezing and remain functional upon thawing. Fully functional in all operational environments. Performance: Treat-to-Drink Time: Ideally less than 5 minutes (target less than 20 minutes). Flow Rate: Not less than 200 mL/min (if applicable). Water Quality: Processed water must be palatable, similar to commercial bottled water. Ease of use with or without gloved hands. Power: Batteries, if used, must be a commercially available type. Microbiological Mitigation: Ideally meets or exceeds requirements of NSF Protocol P248.01 (optional). SECTION 2 - RFI Procedures This RFI is issued to identify interested sources and gather information on market capabilities. Participation is voluntary, and the Government will not reimburse any costs associated with responding. Failure to respond does not preclude participation in any future solicitation. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on SAM.gov. SECTION 3 - Instructions for Information Submissions 3.1 General Guidelines a. Unnecessarily elaborate brochures are not desired. b. Submissions must be sent electronically via email as instructed below. c. The Government will not pay for any information, administrative costs, or product samples submitted in response to this notice. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. 3.2 Information Package Contents Interested parties are invited to submit responses detailing their products, technologies, and capabilities. The submission should include: A description of current commercial product(s) and how they can address the military requirements. Technical information (e.g., technical literature, test data, patents, illustrations). Information regarding the firm's experience, personnel, and facilities. Product cost information. Company information: business size (including socioeconomic status), CAGE code, and applicable NAICS code. GSA Federal Supply Schedule contract number, if applicable. A physical sample (optional; no payment will be made for unsolicited samples). Any relevant data on microbiological or chemical reductions. 3.3 Information Package Submission Responses shall be submitted via e-mail to the following points of contact (POCs): Eric Brack, eric.m.brack.civ@army.mil Parker Brandwein, parker.d.brandwein.civ@army.mil Blaise Liess, blaise.p.liess.civ@army.mil Ronda Hinnant, ronda.r.hinnant.civ@army.mil Responses must be submitted no later than 12 November 2026 by 5:00 p.m. EST. title: Denmark – Industrial machinery – Delivery and installation of a ICP Reactive ion etcher for silicon dielctrics
description: DTU Nanolab wishes to acquire a high ion density source reactive ion etcher for oxides and nitrides of silicon to become its new primary instrument for 150 mm wafer processing. Delivery is expected no later than Q3 2027. The Instrument will be installed in the DTU Nanolab cleanroom - a university facility providing a comprehensive suite of micro- and nanofabrication tools. It serves a diverse community of over 200 active users, ranging from novice students to experienced researchers, as well a high percentage of commercial clients. As an open access tool, the Instrument must support the full spectrum of etching of silicon-based dielectrics, from sub 100 nm nanostructures defined by electron beam lithography to depths of several tens of microns. Meeting these demands requires exceptional process controllability and tunability: the system must perform ultra precise, low-rate etches (< 100 nm/min) with smooth and straight sidewalls and minimal undercut for shallow features, alongside high etch rate deep etches (approaching 500 nm/min). It must also accommodate all silicon dielectrics of the form SixNy, SixOx and SixOyNz, and be compatible with mask materials including Si, Cr, e-beam resists and UV/DUV photoresists with high mask selectivity for all these masking materials. The user interface must be intuitive and user friendly. The Instrument should be engineered to the highest industrial standards to minimize maintenance, and any required servicing must be straightforward and efficient. The instrument must be configured for 150 mm wafer processing and a complete kit enabling the processing of 200 mm wafers must be included in the tender as an option. Furthermore, DTU will have the option to purchase one more ICP Reactive ion etcher for silicon dielctrics identical to the initial instrument.

title: Luxembourg – Evaluation consultancy services – Study for the end-term evaluation of the EU strategic framework on health and safety at work 2021–2027 and support to the preparation of the post-2027 strategic framework
description: This call for tenders is for an external independent study for the end-term evaluation of the EU strategic framework on health and safety at work 2021–2027 and to support the contracting authority in relation to the open public consultation in preparation of the post-2027 strategic framework. The strategic framework sets out three crosscutting key objectives and a range of actions for promoting workers’ health and safety. The three objectives are: anticipating and managing change in the new world of work brought about by the green, digital and demographic transitions; improving prevention of workplace accidents and illnesses; increasing preparedness for any potential future health crises. The implementation of these three objectives is underpinned by: (i) social dialogue; (ii) strengthening of the evidence base; (iii) strengthening of enforcement; (iv) awareness raising; and (v) funding. At its plenary meeting in December 2025, the tripartite Advisory Committee on Safety and Health at Work (ACSH) adopted an opinion on the state of play and future impulses regarding the EU strategic framework on health and safety at work4. Moreover, in June 2026, the Commission adopted the Report on the screening of the EU acquis in the area of health and safety at work5, and its accompanying Staff Working Document6 [TBC]. The results of this screening exercise study will inform the process of developing new EU OSH priorities in the strategic framework on health and safety at work after 2027.

title: Germany – Agricultural services – Beratung landwirtschaftlicher Betriebe zur Erhaltung und Verbesserung der Biodiversität und Nachhaltigkeit in der Landwirtschaft (EB)
description: Für das ML soll eine Rahmenvereinbarung zur Erbringung von Beratungsdienstleistungen nach Art. 78 der EU Strategieplan VO (EU) 2021/2115 vom 2. Dezember 2021 vergeben werden. Ausgeschrieben werden definierte Beratungsdienstleistungen für landwirtschaftliche Betriebe. Die Maßnahme zielt auf die Erhaltung und Verbesserung der Nachhaltigkeit landwirtschaftlicher Betriebe unter besonderer Beachtung der Aspekte der Biodiversität, der Klimaresilienz, des Tierwohls und eines effizienten Umgangs mit Ressourcen durch Wissenstransfer. Die Beratungsleistungen sind nur dann förderfähig, wenn die Beratungen durch nach diesem Vergabeverfahren ausgewählte Beratungsanbieter und Beratungskräfte durchgeführt werden. Nähere Einzelheiten zu Art und Umfang des Auftrags sind der Leistungsbeschreibung - Fachlicher Teil (Teil B) und der Leistungsbeschreibung - Zuwendungsverfahren (Teil C) - sowie den weiteren beigefügten Anlagen zu entnehmen. Die Rahmenvereinbarung soll mit mehreren Unternehmen (§ 21 Abs. 4 Nr. 1 VgV) abgeschlossen werden, um den Landwirten eine Wahl des Beratungsanbieters zu ermöglichen. Dabei werden so viele Zuschläge entsprechend der Platzierung nach der Angebotswertung erteilt, bis die Angebotssummen der bezuschlagten Angebote die zur Verfügung stehende Fördersumme von 5.849.200 EUR im Vertragszeitraum 01. März 2027 - 30. Juni 2029 erreicht ist. Das zuletzt bezuschlagte Angebot wird daher voraussichtlich nicht in vollem Umfang berücksichtigt werden können, sondern nur insoweit bis die zur Verfügung stehenden Fördermittel ausgeschöpft sind. Das maximal mögliche Mittelvolumen je Beratungsanbieter in dem gesamten Vertragszeitraum wird im Rahmen des Vergabeverfahrens ermittelt, wobei je Beratungsanbieter maximal ein Betrag in Höhe von bis zu 300.000 EUR zugeteilt wird. Dieser Betrag kann im Fall einer späteren Zuteilung von gestrichenen Mitteln (s.u.) überschritten werden. Für den Fall, dass ein Beratungsanbieter seinen Betrag nicht benötigt/abruft, werden ihm Mittel gestrichen. Die dann frei gewordenen Mittel können an die anderen Beratungsanbieter zugewiesen werden. Weitere Einzelheiten hierzu finden sich in der Leistungsbeschreibung - Zuwendungsverfahren (Teil C). Der Abschluss der Rahmenvereinbarung bildet zunächst keinen Anspruch auf die Mittel und stellt keine Erteilung einer Zuwendung dar. Hierfür muss im Rahmen des Zuwendungsverfahrens ein separater Förderantrag gestellt und dieser bewilligt werden (siehe hierzu auch Leistungsbeschreibung - Zuwendungsverfahren (Teil C)).

title: Germany – Landscaping work – Stiftung Schloss Marienburg: Bauabschnitt 2: Garten- und Landschaftsbau: Oberbauschichten
description: Die Stiftung Schloss Marienburg beabsichtigt die Sanierung des Schlosses. Das Gebäude ist ein eingetragenes Baudenkmal. Die historische Bausubstanz ist zu schonen und zu erhalten. Die Erfordernisse aus dem Denkmalschutz verlangen von allen am Bau beteiligten Firmen eine besondere Vorsicht und Sorgfalt und eine enge Abstimmung mit der Bauleitung. Sanierung des Schlosses Marienburg, Bauabschnitte 2.1 Hangsicherung und 2.2 Terrasse Süd - Garten- und Landschaftsbauarbeiten zur Herstellung von Oberbauschichten, Pflasterbelägen und Entwässerungsanlagen. Die Leistungen umfassen insbesondere Erdarbeiten, Herstellung von Bodenaufbauten, Ziegelpflaster und wassergebundenen Wegedecken, Abdichtungs- und Dränagearbeiten, Entwässerungsleitungen und -rinnen sowie Entsorgung und Dokumentation. Der zu sanierende Hangbereich besteht aus einer bis zu rund 13 m hohen und bis zu rund 65° gegenüber der Horizontalen geneigten Festgesteinswand aus Buntsandstein. Im oberen Bereich des Hanges befindet sich ein historischer Laubengang, der mittels einer Gewölbekonstruktion auf dem Hang aufgelagert ist. Aufgrund von eindringendem Wasser und Bewuchs haben sich Teile der Felsoberfläche gelöst, wodurch die Auflagerpunkte der tragenden Konsolsteine teilweise nicht mehr vorhanden sind. Der Laubengang wird derzeit durch eine Stahlkonstruktion notabgestützt und ist gesperrt. Im Rahmen der Sanierung wird der Bodenaufbau des Laubengangs einschließlich Pflasterbelag, Abdichtung und Entwässerung erneuert. Im Bauabschnitt 2.2 ist die Nutzbarmachung der Terrasse Süd vorgesehen. Hierzu wird die vorhandene Betonoberfläche zurückgebaut und ein neuer Bodenaufbau mit wassergebundener Wegedecke hergestellt. Bestandteil der Maßnahmen ist außerdem die Erneuerung der Entwässerung sowie die Herstellung der erforderlichen Oberbauschichten auf den Stahlbetondecken. Die Arbeiten erfolgen unter besonderer Berücksichtigung des Denkmalschutzes und der historischen Bausubstanz.
